scope: The review's P1 and all six P2s; historical cloud/timing evidence remains unchanged.

changes.behavior: Collection errors retain one idle failure deadline; missing reservations and permanent source limits interrupt pending execution without passing evidence or fabricated learner activity.
coverage: Repeated collection errors keep the original deadline and stop renewal after grace
Source size/count limits preserve the previous checkpoint on release

changes.requirement: Keep periodic checkpoint I/O outside the Study lock
changes.behavior: Capture/upload uses a checkpoint mutex. Brief Study/environment publication validates the source generation and writers; head and recovery metadata commit in one PostgreSQL transaction.
coverage: Activity succeeds while upload is blocked
Concurrent edits or command reservations reject publication
A second maintenance instance does not duplicate capture
Metadata callback failure rolls back checkpoint head

changes.behavior: Add migration 10 with maintenance_checked_at. Claim least-checked environments with SKIP LOCKED and advance their timestamp before attempting work.
coverage: 105 synthetic bindings visited in two durable scan batches
Shipped migration checksums retained; new checksum pinned

changes.behavior: Lease-only maintenance protects idle timeout plus failure grace and bounded active/recent work. Renewal covers the checkpoint deadline plus margin; expired grace/discard intent gets no extension.
coverage: Queued dirty and clean bindings receive protection
Older idle/overdue, expired grace and discard boundaries remain bounded
Passive and maintenance observation of confirmed dirty expiry records a recovery/loss notice

changes.behavior: PostgreSQL clocks determine inactivity, grace, dirty generation and execution deadlines.
coverage: Date constructor shifted seven days forward/backward cannot change inactivity decisions
First dirty timestamp remains close to database time

changes.behavior: Both built-in and registered lazy byte-store wrappers forward optional write options.
coverage: Two lazy wrapper cancellation contract regressions

changes.requirement: Raise default and document activity semantics
changes.behavior: Default idle timeout is ten minutes; the five-minute operator choice and trusted input/visibility limits are documented.
coverage: Fatal boot validation and browser workspace journey

fixes: Assign first dirty timestamp with PostgreSQL time instead of a skewable Date constructor.
Require current dirty state and expected revision before recording an observed-expiry loss notice.
Reuse periodic capture admission for publication on one-slot Study pools.
Clarify checkpoint-only scope and deferred retention in both READMEs.
selfReview.result: Both reviewers completed final/delta inspection with no remaining confirmed finding. They did not run tests; validation below was run by the coordinating agent.

postgres.provider: Controlled provider and in-memory object storage; actual local Python/Java 17 execution

browser.backend: Browser route fixtures; backend concurrency is covered separately by PostgreSQL tests

validation.packageVersions: Gate passed against the pinned PR base; storage 0.39.0 -> 0.39.1
validation.testHarnessAdjustment: An initial concurrent full run hit the existing one-second archive-start synchronization timeout (118 passed, 1 failed). The isolated scenario passed. Its wait was raised to five seconds with all behavior assertions retained; the complete rerun passed all 119.

limitations: No new paid cloud/model call or wall-clock lifecycle timing measurement was performed in this follow-up.
Historical cloud/S3-compatible storage and timing results remain in the October 23 artifacts.
Unexpected provider/application/storage failure can still lose changes since the latest successful checkpoint.
Broader hosted language/provider billing/deployment/capacity acceptance remains in issues 2008 and 2009; this PR closes 2007, not parent 1995.
